text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Parliament starts review of its performance. Parliament's performance has been criticised as lax by some Kuwaitis.
- Iraq and Iran still a threat to the region, U.S. official visiting the Gulf says.
- Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah resumes work in London, treatment almost completed, said Defence Minister Sheikh Salem Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah said.
- Communications, Electricity and Water Minister Jassem al-Oun says bid to replace expatriate state workers with nationals has been launched.
- Kuwaiti Islamic finance firm, The International Investor, to take part in new real estate company to be established in two months.
- Iran leads diplomatic drive on Jerusalem.
- Kuwaiti businessman donates $10,000 to Jordanian soldier's mother. The soldier opened fire last week on Israeli schoolgirls killing seven.
- Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati says Iran does not seek conflict in the region.
- Sharp rise in venereal diseases in Kuwait during the past two years, Health Ministry sources say.
